title: Accident Reporting
summary: Employers must report every work-related death to OSHA within 8 hours, and every in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye within 24 hours.
talking_points: A work-related death must be reported to OSHA within 8 hours.
An in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye must be reported to OSHA within 24 hours.
Report by phone to the nearest OSHA Area Office, by phone to 1-800-321-OSHA (1-800-321-6742), or online at www.osha.gov.
If the Area Office is closed, use the 800 number or the online reporting application. Voicemail, fax, and email do not count.
Good practice, not an OSHA requirement: tell your supervisor right away after any serious injury so the employer can meet the report deadline.
OSHA needs the site name, incident location and time, type of event, number and names of employees hurt, a contact person and phone number, and a brief description.
A motor vehicle crash in a construction work zone must be reported. A hospital stay for observation or diagnostic testing only does not have to be reported.
A death only has to be reported if it occurs within 30 days of the incident. A hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye only has to be reported if it occurs within 24 hours of the incident.
site_hazards_to_check: No posted contact number or person to make the OSHA report
Crew who do not know to tell the supervisor right away after a serious injury
Incident details (time, location, names) not written down quickly
Unclear who makes the report if the supervisor is away
discussion_questions: Who calls OSHA on this site, and what number do they use?
What counts as an amputation for reporting, and does a fingertip count?
What information do we need ready when we make the call?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA published material. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: Verified every point against 29 CFR 1904.39 text: 8 h death, 24 h in-patient hospitalization/amputation/loss of eye, three reporting methods, no voicemail/fax/email, required info list, construction work zone motor vehicle crash, observation-only stays, 30-day/24-hour limits. Part 1904 applies to construction.

FIX: 'Tell your supervisor right away' is not in the source; reworded as labelled good practice so it is not presented as an OSHA requirement. Same for the matching hazard/question wording (left as-is, generic).
Non-blocking: legal thresholds are stated as employer duties; the talk should be paired with the company's own reporting procedure.
